newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway premier vows to fight bikers after bombing.
newsitem.headline: Norway premier vows to fight bikers after bombing.

text.p: Norwegian Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland vowed on Thursday to crack down on motorcycle gangs after a woman bystander was killed in the bombing of a bike gang's clubhouse.
Jagland visited Drammen, a town 40 km (25 Miles) south of Oslo, following the incident in which a bomb was set off in a car parked next to the clubhouse of the Bandidos biker gang late on Wednesday.
The first explosion, which was followed by more detonations minutes later in the clubhouse, killed a 51-year-old woman who was driving past the building, police said.
Police said four people were taken to hospital suffering from shock, cuts and the effects of smoke inhalation. Windows in homes within several hundred metres were smashed.
"This part of the street looks like Bosnia," Jagland told Norwegian NRK television after inspecting the site of the attack.

"To stuff a car with explosives, park it in the street like this and not think that innocent people may be hurt and killed. These are anti-humans. They deserve no better description. They are killers and shall be punished according to the rule of law," he said.

Police would not speculate who bombed the three-story building, which collapsed in flames, but the Norwegian media said it was the latest episode in a turf war between rival biker gangs in the Nordic region.
Over the past three years at least eight people have been killed in Sweden, Denmark, Norway and Finland in fights between the rival Hells Angels and Bandidos gangs, both offshoots of U.S. bike clans.
"Everything indicates the explosion was an act of revenge from the Hells Angels," Norwegian TV2 television said.
NRK television aired an amateur video it said showed three Bandidos members in their underwear in the street after fleeing the blazing building.

Jagland said Norway planned to copy a law introduced last year by neighbouring Denmark to drive biker clubhouses out of urban areas, where other residents fear being caught in the crossfire in battles between their unwanted neighbours.
